The Three Siblings

DM, ERP, and Consolidation get confused constantly — because they're related, but they are not the same job.

🍳 Think of a restaurant. ERP is the kitchen where every branch preps its own ingredients — invoices, payroll, ledger entries. Consolidation is the head chef combining ingredients from every branch kitchen into one final dish — the group's numbers, eliminations and currency translation done. DM (Disclosure Management) is the plating and presentation — turning that finished dish into something you'd actually serve to a regulator, a board, or the public markets. Same meal, three completely different jobs.
🏭

ERP

The system of record for transactions — invoices, payroll, master data, the general ledger.

Is
Where transactions live
Isn't
A filing tool, a consolidation engine
Example tools
SAP · Oracle · Dynamics 365
🧮

Consolidation

Combining every entity's books into one group number — eliminations, FX translation, minority interest.

Is
The group math
Isn't
A public-facing document, a transaction system
Example tools
Oracle Hyperion · OneStream · Board · Tagetik
📑

DM (Disclosure Mgmt)

Turning the final, consolidated number into a filed, tagged, audited document — annual report, XBRL, ESG.

Is
The filed, public output
Isn't
A number-cruncher, a ledger
Example tools
IRIS Carbon · Workiva · DFIN

🎯 How to draw the line in a customer conversation

"Does IRIS Carbon replace our ERP?"
No — we don't touch transactions or the ledger. That's ERP's job, always will be.
"We already consolidate in Hyperion/OneStream/Board — why do we need you?"
Those tools compute your consolidated numbers. We take that final number into a collaborative workspace — where your team drafts, reviews with built-in checks, and embedded AI assists throughout — then auto-tags it, so the document is ready to file directly with the regulator, or ready for public and internal consumption.
"Isn't this all the same thing?"
Three jobs, three owners, three moments in the calendar: ERP runs all year, Consolidation runs at close, DM runs right before filing. We only ever show up at the very last one.

Grounding It in a Real Company

Different vendor, different job, same company.

🔋 NHOA
ERP: SAP→ Consolidation: Board→ DM: IRIS Carbon
Three different vendors, three different jobs, one company. SAP runs the transactions, Board does the group math, and when it's time to actually file — that's us.
The pattern that matters It doesn't matter whether the ERP underneath is SAP, Oracle, or Dynamics, or whether the consolidation tool is Board, Hyperion, or OneStream — every one of these companies still needs the same last step: turning that consolidated number into a filed, tagged, audited disclosure. That's exactly where IRIS Carbon sits, regardless of what's running underneath.
